df3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_82/training_3.csv", index_col=0)

# UNION all source tables (schemas are identical)
df_union = pd.concat([df0, df1, df2, df3], ignore_index=True)

# GroupBy columns:
# From target schema and hints:
# Leftmost columns that are string or integer and appear unique or identifying:
# categories (string), completed (bool), copyright (int), cover (string), cover_timestamp (string),
# createDate (string), deleted (bool), description (string), firstPartId (int),
# firstPublishedPart.createDate (string), firstPublishedPart.id (int), id (int),
# language.id (int), language.name (string), lastPublishedPart.createDate (string),
# lastPublishedPart.id (int), mature (bool), modifyDate (string), numParts (int),
# parts (string), rating (int), tags (string), title (string), url (string),
# user.avatar (string), user.fullname (string), user.name (string)

group_by_cols = [
    'categories', 'completed', 'copyright', 'cover', 'cover_timestamp', 'createDate', 'deleted',
    'description', 'firstPartId', 'firstPublishedPart.createDate', 'firstPublishedPart.id', 'id',
    'language.id', 'language.name', 'lastPublishedPart.createDate', 'lastPublishedPart.id',
    'mature', 'modifyDate', 'numParts', 'parts', 'rating', 'tags', 'title', 'url',
    'user.avatar', 'user.fullname', 'user.name'
]

# Aggregation columns: commentCount, readCount, voteCount
# Use sum aggregation as these are counts and sums in target examples

agg_dict = {
    'commentCount': 'sum',
    'readCount': 'sum',
    'voteCount': 'sum'
}

# Perform groupby and aggregation
df_final = df_union.groupby(group_by_cols, dropna=False, as_index=False).agg(agg_dict)

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
target_columns = [
    'categories', 'commentCount', 'completed', 'copyright', 'cover', 'cover_timestamp', 'createDate',
    'deleted', 'description', 'firstPartId', 'firstPublishedPart.createDate', 'firstPublishedPart.id',
    'id', 'language.id', 'language.name', 'lastPublishedPart.createDate', 'lastPublishedPart.id',
    'length', 'mature', 'modifyDate', 'numParts', 'parts', 'rating', 'readCount', 'tags', 'title',
    'url', 'user.avatar', 'user.fullname', 'user.name', 'voteCount'
]

# Note: 'length' column is not in group_by or aggregation, so it will be lost in groupby.
# We must handle 'length' column:
# Since 'length' is integer and appears in target schema, but not aggregated,
# and it varies per id, we can take first() per group (since id is in group_by, length should be unique per id)
# So we add length to group_by columns or aggregate it by first()

# Add 'length' to group_by columns to preserve it (it is integer and leftmost after id)
# But 'length' is after lastPublishedPart.id in target schema, so we can add it to group_by safely

# Update group_by_cols to include 'length'
group_by_cols_with_length = group_by_cols + ['length']

# Re-aggregate with length included in group_by to preserve it
df_final = df_union.groupby(group_by_cols_with_length, dropna=False, as_index=False).agg(agg_dict)

# Reorder columns again
df_final = df_final[target_columns]

# Write output CSV
df_final.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_82/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
